source: Find the Hidden Numbers
A box multiplies by a secret number. The numbers 30, 42, 54

items.question: A box multiplies by a secret number. The numbers 30, 42, 54 and 90 come out. Find every number the box might multiply by, and the numbers that went in for the biggest one.
steps: Try 4: 7 × 4 = 28 and 8 × 4 = 32, so 30 is not a multiple of 4. So 4 does not work.
Try 5: 8 × 5 = 40 and 9 × 5 = 45, so 42 is not a multiple of 5. So 5 does not work.
The numbers from 7 to 30 are checked the same way and none of them fits all four numbers. For example 10 does not fit: 4 × 10 = 40 and 5 × 10 = 50, so 42 is not a multiple of 10.
The multipliers 1, 2, 3 and 6 are the common factors of 30, 42, 54 and 90, and the four numbers are multiples of each of them.
Check: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30, a product of factors that gives a multiple.
items.answer: The box might multiply by 1, 2, 3 or 6. For 6, the numbers 5, 7, 9 and 15 went in

videos.answer: The box might multiply by 1, 2, 3 or 6. For 6, the numbers 5, 7, 9 and 15 went in

source: Find the hidden numbers: guess the multiplier

items.question: Numbers put in this box get multiplied by a number and come out. Four numbers come out of the box: 28, 36, 48 and 72. (a): Can you guess the multiplier if you see the 4 numbers coming out of the box? (b): Is there more than one possible multiplier? (c): What numbers might have been put inside the box? Share your thoughts in the class.
steps: The box multiplied each number that went in, so every number that comes out is a multiple of the multiplier.
Try 4: 28 ÷ 4 = 7, 36 ÷ 4 = 9, 48 ÷ 4 = 12 and 72 ÷ 4 = 18. All four are whole numbers, so 4 can be the multiplier.
Try 2: 28 ÷ 2 = 14, 36 ÷ 2 = 18, 48 ÷ 2 = 24 and 72 ÷ 2 = 36. So 2 can be the multiplier too.
Try 1: the numbers that went in are 28, 36, 48 and 72 themselves. So 1 works too.
Try 3: 9 × 3 = 27 and 10 × 3 = 30, so 28 is not a multiple of 3. So 3 does not work.

(a): the multiplier can be 4. (b): yes, 1, 2 and 4 all work. They are the common factors of 28, 36, 48 and 72. (c): Sample answer: with multiplier 4 the numbers 7, 9, 12 and 18 went in. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: (a): 4 (2 and 1 work too). (b): Yes, 1, 2 and 4. (c): Sample answer: 7, 9, 12 and 18 went in with 4. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: (a): 4 (2 and 1 work too). (b): Yes, 1, 2 and 4. (c): Sample answer: 7, 9, 12 and 18 went in with 4. Your answer may differ.

source: You have 18 square tiles. Make every array of 18 tiles and l

items.question: You have 18 square tiles. Make every array of 18 tiles and list the factors of 18.
steps: Try 1 row: all 18 tiles in one row. 1 × 18 = 18, so the array is 1 × 18.
Try 2 rows: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 tiles in each row. 2 × 9 = 18, so the array is 2 × 9.
Try 3 rows: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 tiles in each row. 3 × 6 = 18, so the array is 3 × 6.
Try 4 rows: 4 × 4 = 16 and 4 × 5 = 20, so 18 tiles cannot fill 4 equal rows. 4 is not a factor.
Try 5 rows: 5 × 3 = 15 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 5 is not a factor either.
Try 6 rows: 6 × 3 = 18. This is the 3 × 6 array turned round, so it gives no new factor.
Write the numbers from the arrays: 1, 18, 2, 9, 3 and 6. In order they are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18.
Check: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so both divide 18 completely.
items.answer: The arrays are 1 × 18, 2 × 9 and 3 × 6. The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18

videos.answer: The arrays are 1 × 18, 2 × 9 and 3 × 6. The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18

source: Show that 44 is a multiple of each of its factors 1, 2, 4, 1

items.question: Show that 44 is a multiple of each of its factors 1, 2, 4, 11, 22 and 44. Is 44 a multiple of 8?
steps: Write the arrays of 44: 1 × 44 = 44, 2 × 22 = 44 and 4 × 11 = 44.
Each multiplication is a factor times a whole number that makes 44. So 44 is a multiple of 1, 44, 2, 22, 4 and 11.
The number itself: 44 × 1 = 44, so 44 is a multiple of itself.
Is 44 a multiple of 8? 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 6 = 48. 44 is between them, so 8 is not a factor of 44 and 44 is not a multiple of 8.
Check: 44 ÷ 4 = 11 and 44 ÷ 22 = 2, both exact.
items.answer: 44 is a multiple of each of 1, 2, 4, 11, 22 and 44, but not of 8

videos.answer: 44 is a multiple of each of 1, 2, 4, 11, 22 and 44, but not of 8

source: How many arrays can you make with 19 tiles and with 21 tiles

items.question: How many arrays can you make with 19 tiles and with 21 tiles? Which of the two numbers is a prime number?
steps: 19 tiles: 1 row of 19 gives the array 1 × 19, because 1 × 19 = 19.
Try 2 rows: 2 × 9 = 18 and 2 × 10 = 20, so 19 tiles cannot fill 2 equal rows.
Try 3, 4 and 5 rows in the same way: 3 × 6 = 18 and 3 × 7 = 21; 4 × 4 = 16 and 4 × 5 = 20; 5 × 3 = 15 and 5 × 4 = 20. None of them makes 19.
No number of rows from 2 to 18 makes 19, so 19 has only the array 1 × 19 and only the factors 1 and 19.
21 tiles: 1 × 21 = 21 and 3 × 7 = 21, so 21 has the arrays 1 × 21 and 3 × 7 and the four factors 1, 3, 7 and 21.
19 has only two factors, so 19 is a prime number. 21 has four factors, so it is not.
Check: 3 × 7 = 21, but no multiplication of two numbers bigger than 1 makes 19.
items.answer: 19 makes only the array 1 × 19, so it is a prime number. 21 makes 1 × 21 and 3 × 7, so it is not

videos.answer: 19 makes only the array 1 × 19, so it is a prime number. 21 makes 1 × 21 and 3 × 7, so it is not

source: Arrays: other arrays for 15

items.question: A number, when arranged in an array, shows the factors of that number. Are there other numbers that are factors of 15? Try to make other arrays for the number 15.
steps: The array in your maths book has 3 rows of 5 tiles: 3 × 5 = 15. So 3 and 5 are factors of 15.
Try 1 row: all 15 tiles in one row. 1 × 15 = 15. So 1 and 15 are factors of 15.
Try 2 rows: 2 × 7 = 14 and 2 × 8 = 16, so 15 tiles cannot fill 2 equal rows. 2 is not a factor.
Try 4 rows: 4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16, so 4 is not a factor either.
5 rows of 3 is the same array as 3 rows of 5, turned round: 5 × 3 = 15.
Check: 15 ÷ 1 = 15, 15 ÷ 3 = 5, 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 15 ÷ 15 = 1. Each division is exact.
items.answer: Yes. 1 and 15, from the array 1 × 15. The factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5 and 15.

videos.answer: Yes. 1 and 15, from the array 1 × 15. The factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5 and 15.

source: Arrays: why 12 is a multiple of its factors

items.question: Do you see why 12 is a multiple of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12? (a): 2 × ___ = 12; (b): 3 × ___ = 12; (c): 12 × ___ = 12; (d): 1 × ___ = 12
steps: (a): 2 × 6 = 12, so the blank is 6. 12 is six 2s.
(b): 3 × 4 = 12, so the blank is 4.
(c): 12 × 1 = 12, so the blank is 1. The number itself is always a multiple of itself.
(d): 1 × 12 = 12, so the blank is 12. 1 is a factor of every number.
In each line a factor times a whole number makes 12, so 12 is a multiple of each of its factors.

source: Let Us Do (arrays), Q1

items.question: Make different arrays for the following numbers. Identify the factors in each case. (a): 10; (b): 14; (c): 13; (d): 20; (e): 25; (f): 32; (g): 37; (h): 46; (i): 54
steps: (a): 10 has the arrays 1 × 10 and 2 × 5. Factors: 1, 2, 5, 10.
(b): 14 has the arrays 1 × 14 and 2 × 7. Factors: 1, 2, 7, 14.
(c): 13 has only the array 1 × 13. Factors: 1, 13.
(d): 20 has the arrays 1 × 20, 2 × 10 and 4 × 5. Factors: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20.
(e): 25 has the arrays 1 × 25 and 5 × 5. Factors: 1, 5, 25. The factor 5 counts once.
(f): 32 has the arrays 1 × 32, 2 × 16 and 4 × 8. Factors: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
(g): 37 has only the array 1 × 37. Factors: 1, 37.
(h): 46 has the arrays 1 × 46 and 2 × 23. Factors: 1, 2, 23, 46.
items.answer: Number of factors: (a): 4; (b): 4; (c): 2; (d): 6; (e): 3; (f): 6; (g): 2; (h): 4; (i): 8. The factors are listed in the steps.

source: Arrays: why 13 and 37 are called prime numbers

items.question: Numbers like 13 and 37 are called prime numbers. Why?
steps: Make the arrays of 13: only 1 row of 13 works, so the only array is 1 × 13. The factors of 13 are 1 and 13.
Make the arrays of 37: only 1 row of 37 works, so the only array is 1 × 37. The factors of 37 are 1 and 37.
Each of them has only two factors, 1 and the number itself.
A number that has only two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. That is why 13 and 37 are prime numbers.
Check: 14 has 4 factors (1, 2, 7, 14), so 14 is not a prime number.
items.answer: Because each has only two factors, 1 and the number itself, and only one array: 1 × 13 and 1 × 37.

videos.answer: Because each has only two factors, 1 and the number itself, and only one array: 1 × 13 and 1 × 37.

source: Robby the rabbit jumps 2 at a time and Deeku the deer jumps

items.question: Robby the rabbit jumps 2 at a time and Deeku the deer jumps 5 at a time. Both start at 0. Which numbers up to 30 will both of them touch?
steps: Deeku touches the multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
The numbers in both lists are 10, 20 and 30. These are the common multiples of 2 and 5 up to 30.
10 is the first common multiple: 2 × 5 = 10, and Robby needs 5 jumps while Deeku needs 2.
Check: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4, both exact, so 20 is a multiple of both.
items.answer: 10, 20 and 30. The first common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10

videos.answer: 10, 20 and 30. The first common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10

source: Robby jumps 6 at a time and Deeku jumps 15 at a time from 0.

items.question: Robby jumps 6 at a time and Deeku jumps 15 at a time from 0. Find three numbers both touch, and say what you notice.
steps: Deeku touches 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90.
The numbers in both lists are 30, 60 and 90. The first common multiple is 30.
30 + 30 = 60 and 60 + 30 = 90, so each common multiple is 30 more than the one before.
30 × 1 = 30, 30 × 2 = 60 and 30 × 3 = 90, so they are the multiples of the first common multiple, 30.
items.answer: 30, 60 and 90. They are the multiples of 30, the first common multiple

videos.answer: 30, 60 and 90. They are the multiples of 30, the first common multiple

source: Animal Jumps: more common multiples of 3 and 4

items.question: 12 is the first common multiple of 3 and 4. What are some other common multiples of 3 and 4? You can continue the number line or take help from the times tables of 3 and 4.
steps: The numbers in both lists are 12, 24, 36 and 48.
Keep going: 4 × 15 = 60 and 3 × 20 = 60, so 60 is a common multiple too.
The common multiples are 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 and so on. Each one is 12 more than the one before.
Check: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 and 36 ÷ 4 = 9, both exact.
items.answer: 24, 36, 48, 60 and so on: the multiples of 12.

videos.answer: 24, 36, 48, 60 and so on: the multiples of 12.

source: Animal Jumps: common multiples of 4 and 6

items.question: Let us write the multiples of two numbers, 4 and 6. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, ... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, ... 12 and 24 are two of the common multiples of 4 and 6. List a few more.
steps: The numbers in both lists are 12, 24, 36 and 48. Your maths book gave 12 and 24, so a few more are 36 and 48.
Check: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 36 ÷ 6 = 6, both exact.
items.answer: 36, 48, 60 and 72: the multiples of 12.

source: Let Us Do (common multiples), Q1

items.question: Find 5 common multiples of the following pairs of numbers. (a): 2 and 3; (b): 5 and 8; (c): 2 and 4; (d): 3 and 9; (e): 5 and 10; (f): 9 and 12; (g): 8 and 12; (h): 6 and 8; (i): 6 and 9
steps: (a): the first common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6 (2 × 3 = 6). Five common multiples: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30.
(b): the multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, and 40 is the first one that is also a multiple of 5 (5 × 8 = 40). Five common multiples: 40, 80, 120, 160, 200.
(c): 4 is a multiple of 2, so the common multiples are the multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20.
(d): 9 is a multiple of 3, so the common multiples are the multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45.
(e): 10 is a multiple of 5, so the common multiples are the multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.
(f): the multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, and 36 is also a multiple of 9 (9 × 4 = 36). Five common multiples: 36, 72, 108, 144, 180.
(g): 24 is a multiple of both (8 × 3 = 24 and 12 × 2 = 24). Five common multiples: 24, 48, 72, 96, 120.
(h): 24 is a multiple of both (6 × 4 = 24 and 8 × 3 = 24). Five common multiples: 24, 48, 72, 96, 120.
(i): 18 is a multiple of both (6 × 3 = 18 and 9 × 2 = 18). Five common multiples: 18, 36, 54, 72, 90.
items.answer: Sample answer, the first common multiple: (a): 6; (b): 40; (c): 4; (d): 9; (e): 10; (f): 36; (g): 24; (h): 24; (i): 18. Add its next multiples. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer, the first common multiple: (a): 6; (b): 40; (c): 4; (d): 9; (e): 10; (f): 36; (g): 24; (h): 24; (i): 18. Add its next multiples. Your answer may differ.

source: Let Us Do (common multiples), Q2

items.question: Food is available at the end of a cobbled road. Robby, the rabbit, takes a jump of 4 each time. Deeku, the deer, takes a jump of 6 each time. They both start at 0. Will both Robby and Deeku reach the food? Who will reach first? How do you know? Explain your answer.
steps: The stones of the road are numbered 0 to 64 and the food is at the end of the road, so each animal must land on stone 64.
Robby jumps 4 at a time and lands on the multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, ..., 60, 64. 4 × 16 = 64, so Robby lands on 64 after 16 jumps.
Deeku jumps 6 at a time and lands on the multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, ..., 54, 60, 66. 6 × 10 = 60 and 6 × 11 = 66, so Deeku lands on 60 and then jumps past 64 to 66.
64 is a multiple of 4 but not a multiple of 6, so only Robby reaches the food.
Robby reaches the food first, because Deeku does not land on it at all. Together they land on 12, 24, 36, 48 and 60, the common multiples of 4 and 6.
Check: 16 × 4 = 64, but 64 is not in the multiples of 6 (6 × 10 = 60 and 6 × 11 = 66).
items.answer: No, only Robby reaches the food: 64 = 4 × 16, but 64 is not a multiple of 6. Robby is first.

videos.answer: No, only Robby reaches the food: 64 = 4 × 16, but 64 is not a multiple of 6. Robby is first.

source: Mowgli jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. Which of the places 8

items.question: Mowgli jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. Which of the places 8, 14, 20 and 26 can he land on? What can you say about 4 and the places he lands on?
steps: His landing places are the multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28.
8 is on the list: 4 × 2 = 8, so he lands on 8 after 2 jumps.
14 is not on the list: he lands on 12 and then on 16, so he skips 14.
20 is on the list: 4 × 5 = 20, so he lands on 20 after 5 jumps.
26 is not on the list: he lands on 24 and then on 28, so he skips 26.
4 divides 8 and 20 completely, so 4 is a common factor of 8 and 20.
Check: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5, both exact.
items.answer: He lands on 8 and 20, and skips 14 and 26. 4 is a common factor of 8 and 20

videos.answer: He lands on 8 and 20, and skips 14 and 26. 4 is a common factor of 8 and 20

source: Find the common factors of 18 and 30, and say which jump siz

items.question: Find the common factors of 18 and 30, and say which jump sizes reach both numbers.
steps: List the factors of 18 from its arrays 1 × 18, 2 × 9 and 3 × 6: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.
List the factors of 30 from its arrays 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10 and 5 × 6: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30.
Pick the numbers that are in both lists: 1, 2, 3 and 6.
Each of these is a jump size that lands on both 18 and 30. Jumps of 6 land on 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. Jumps of 9 land on 18 but skip 30: 9, 18, 27, 36.
1 is always a common factor, because a jump of 1 lands on every number.
Check: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5, both exact.
items.answer: The common factors of 18 and 30 are 1, 2, 3 and 6

videos.answer: The common factors of 18 and 30 are 1, 2, 3 and 6

source: Let Us Do (jumps and factors), Q3

items.question: Mowgli's friends live along the trail on the marked places below. Which of his friends will he be able to visit, if he jumps by 2 steps starting from 0?
steps: Jumps of 2 from 0 land on 2, 4, 6, 8 and so on: the even numbers, the multiples of 2.
The friends live at these places: ant 4, spider 9, frog 12, bird 14, Kaa 21, Sher Khan 25, Baloo 30, Akela 35, deer 39, rabbit 50, monkey 57.
4 = 2 × 2, 12 = 2 × 6, 14 = 2 × 7, 30 = 2 × 15 and 50 = 2 × 25, so a jump of 2 lands on all five of these places.
9, 21, 25, 35, 39 and 57 are odd numbers, so jumps of 2 skip them.
Mowgli can visit the ant, the frog, the bird, Baloo and the rabbit. 2 is a common factor of 4, 12, 14, 30 and 50.
Check: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 and 50 ÷ 2 = 25, both exact.
items.answer: The ant (4), frog (12), bird (14), Baloo (30) and rabbit (50): 2 is a common factor of 4, 12, 14, 30 and 50.

videos.answer: The ant (4), frog (12), bird (14), Baloo (30) and rabbit (50): 2 is a common factor of 4, 12, 14, 30 and 50.

source: Mowgli's Trail: jumps of 3 steps

items.question: Which of his friends will he be able to meet if he jumps by 3 steps? 3 is a common factor of the numbers ___.
steps: Jumps of 3 from 0 land on 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30 and so on: the multiples of 3.
The places 4, 14, 25, 35 and 50 are not multiples of 3, so he jumps over them.
He meets the spider, the frog, Kaa, Baloo, the deer and the monkey.
Check: 39 ÷ 3 = 13 and 57 ÷ 3 = 19, both exact.
items.answer: The spider (9), frog (12), Kaa (21), Baloo (30), deer (39) and monkey (57): 3 is a common factor of 9, 12, 21, 30, 39 and 57.

videos.answer: The spider (9), frog (12), Kaa (21), Baloo (30), deer (39) and monkey (57): 3 is a common factor of 9, 12, 21, 30, 39 and 57.

source: Mowgli's Trail: jumps of 5 steps

items.question: Which numbers will he touch if he jumps by 5 steps? ___. 5 is a common factor of the numbers ___.
steps: Jumps of 5 from 0 touch 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 and 60. The trail ends at 60.
Friends on these numbers: 25 = 5 × 5 (Sher Khan), 30 = 5 × 6 (Baloo), 35 = 5 × 7 (Akela) and 50 = 5 × 10 (the rabbit).
No other friend is on a multiple of 5: 4, 9, 12, 14, 21, 39 and 57 are not.
So he touches 5, 10, 15, ..., 60, and 5 is a common factor of the friends' numbers 25, 30, 35 and 50.
Check: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7, both exact.
items.answer: He touches 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 and 60. 5 is a common factor of 25, 30, 35 and 50.

videos.answer: He touches 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 and 60. 5 is a common factor of 25, 30, 35 and 50.

source: Mowgli's Trail: jumps of 10 steps

items.question: Which numbers will he touch if he jumps by 10 steps? ___. 10 is a common factor of the numbers ___.
steps: Jumps of 10 from 0 touch 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. The trail ends at 60.
Friends on these numbers: 30 = 10 × 3 (Baloo) and 50 = 10 × 5 (the rabbit).
No other friend is on a multiple of 10.
Check: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 and 50 ÷ 10 = 5, both exact.
items.answer: He touches 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. 10 is a common factor of 30 and 50.

videos.answer: He touches 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. 10 is a common factor of 30 and 50.

source: Let Us Do (jumps and factors), Q4

items.question: Let us find some common factors of the numbers 24 and 36. Note that all jumps in the following questions start from 0. (a): Can we jump by 2 steps at a time to reach both 24 and 36? Yes/No. 2 is/is not a common factor of 24 and 36. (b): Can we jump by 3 steps at a time to reach both 24 and 36? Yes/No. 3 is/is not a common factor of 24 and 36. (c): Can we jump by 4 steps at a time to reach both 24 and 36? Yes/No. 4 is/is not a common factor of 24 and 36. (d): What other jumps can we take to reach both 24 and 36? (e): How many common factors can you find for 24 and 36? List them. (f): What about jumping by 1 step each time to reach both 24 and 36?
steps: (a): 2 × 12 = 24 and 2 × 18 = 36, so jumps of 2 reach both. Yes, 2 is a common factor of 24 and 36.
(b): 3 × 8 = 24 and 3 × 12 = 36, so jumps of 3 reach both. Yes, 3 is a common factor.
(c): 4 × 6 = 24 and 4 × 9 = 36, so jumps of 4 reach both. Yes, 4 is a common factor.

(d): jumps of 6 reach both (6 × 4 = 24 and 6 × 6 = 36) and so do jumps of 12 (12 × 2 = 24 and 12 × 3 = 36). Jumps of 8 reach 24 but not 36, and jumps of 9 reach 36 but not 24. The other jumps are 1, 6 and 12.
(e): the factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. In both lists: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. That is 6 common factors.
(f): a jump of 1 lands on every number: 1 × 24 = 24 and 1 × 36 = 36. Yes, 1 is a common factor of 24 and 36.
Check: 12 × 2 = 24 and 12 × 3 = 36, so 12, the biggest common factor, reaches both.
items.answer: (a): Yes; (b): Yes; (c): Yes; (d): 1, 6 and 12; (e): 6 common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; (f): Yes, 1 is a common factor.

videos.answer: (a): Yes; (b): Yes; (c): Yes; (d): 1, 6 and 12; (e): 6 common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; (f): Yes, 1 is a common factor.

source: Let Us Do (jumps and factors), Q5

items.question: What are the common factors of 12 and 13?
steps: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
13 has only the array 1 × 13, so its factors are 1 and 13.
The only number in both lists is 1.
1 and the number itself are always factors of any number, so 1 is always a common factor.
Check: a jump of 3 lands on 12 (3 × 4 = 12) but not on 13, because the next landing is 15.
items.answer: Only 1. The common factor of 12 and 13 is 1.

videos.answer: Only 1. The common factor of 12 and 13 is 1.

source: Let Us Do (jumps and factors), Q6

items.question: Find which of the following numbers can be reached by jumps of 4 steps? 4 is the common factor of the numbers ___.
steps: Jumps of 4 land on the multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48.
10 is not a multiple of 4: 4 × 2 = 8 and 4 × 3 = 12, so the jumps go from 8 to 12 and skip 10.
16 = 4 × 4, so a jump of 4 reaches 16.
27 is not a multiple of 4: 4 × 6 = 24 and 4 × 7 = 28, so 27 is skipped.
36 = 4 × 9 and 48 = 4 × 12, so both can be reached. 0 is the starting place.
Check: 16 ÷ 4 = 4, 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 48 ÷ 4 = 12, all exact.
items.answer: 16, 36 and 48 can be reached. 4 is a common factor of 16, 36 and 48.

videos.answer: 16, 36 and 48 can be reached. 4 is a common factor of 16, 36 and 48.

source: Let Us Do (jumps and factors), Q7

items.question: Find the common factors of the following pairs of numbers. (a): 12 and 16; (b): 8 and 12; (c): 4 and 16; (d): 2 and 9; (e): 3 and 5; (f): 12 and 15; (g): 20 and 5; (h): 9 and 21; (i): 6 and 27
steps: (a): the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 and of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Common: 1, 2, 4.
(b): the factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, 8 and of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Common: 1, 2, 4.
(c): the factors of 4 are 1, 2, 4 and of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Common: 1, 2, 4.
(d): the factors of 2 are 1, 2 and of 9 are 1, 3, 9. Common: 1.
(e): the factors of 3 are 1, 3 and of 5 are 1, 5. Common: 1.
(f): the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 and of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15. Common: 1, 3.
(g): the factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20 and of 5 are 1, 5. Common: 1, 5.
(h): the factors of 9 are 1, 3, 9 and of 21 are 1, 3, 7, 21. Common: 1, 3.
(i): the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3, 6 and of 27 are 1, 3, 9, 27. Common: 1, 3.
Check: 4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16, so jumps of 4 reach both 12 and 16; 3 × 3 = 9 and 3 × 7 = 21, so jumps of 3 reach both 9 and 21.

source: Check two statements. (1) Every multiple of 4 is also a mult

items.question: Check two statements. (1) Every multiple of 4 is also a multiple of 2. (2) Every multiple of 6 is also a multiple of 4.
steps: (1): write some multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Each one is also a multiple of 2: 2 × 2 = 4, 2 × 4 = 8, 2 × 6 = 12, 2 × 8 = 16 and 2 × 10 = 20.
Why it always works: 4 = 2 × 2, so every multiple of 4 is made of 2s. Statement (1) is true.
(2): write some multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. 12 and 24 are multiples of 4 (4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 6 = 24), but 6 is not: 4 × 1 = 4 and 4 × 2 = 8.
One multiple of 6 that is not a multiple of 4 is enough. 6 is one, so statement (2) is false.
Check: 18 is another example. 4 × 4 = 16 and 4 × 5 = 20, so 18 is not a multiple of 4.
items.answer: (1) is true because 4 = 2 × 2. (2) is false: 6 is a multiple of 6 but not of 4

items.question: Sort the numbers 16, 35, 60, 48, 85 and 70 into: divisible by 2 only, divisible by 5 only, and divisible by 2, 5 and 10.
steps: 16: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 exactly. 5 × 3 = 15 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 16 is not divisible by 5. 16 is divisible by 2 only.
35: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 exactly. 2 × 17 = 34 and 2 × 18 = 36, so 35 is not divisible by 2. 35 is divisible by 5 only.
60: 60 ÷ 2 = 30, 60 ÷ 5 = 12 and 60 ÷ 10 = 6, all exact. 60 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10.
48: 48 ÷ 2 = 24 exactly. 5 × 9 = 45 and 5 × 10 = 50, so 48 is not divisible by 5. 48 is divisible by 2 only.
85: 85 ÷ 5 = 17 exactly. 2 × 42 = 84 and 2 × 43 = 86, so 85 is not divisible by 2. 85 is divisible by 5 only.
70: 70 ÷ 2 = 35, 70 ÷ 5 = 14 and 70 ÷ 10 = 7, all exact. 70 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10.
No number is divisible by 10 only: 60 and 70 are divisible by 10, and both are also divisible by 2 and 5.
items.answer: 2 only: 16 and 48. 5 only: 35 and 85. 2, 5 and 10: 60 and 70. None is divisible by 10 only

videos.answer: 2 only: 16 and 48. 5 only: 35 and 85. 2, 5 and 10: 60 and 70. None is divisible by 10 only

items.question: State whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F). (a): Factors of even numbers must be even. (b): Multiples of odd numbers cannot be even. (c): Factors of odd numbers cannot be even. (d): One of the common multiples of two consecutive numbers is their product. (e): The only common factor of any two consecutive numbers is 1. (f): 0 cannot be a factor of any number.
steps: (a): False. 12 is even, and 3 is a factor of 12 (3 × 4 = 12), but 3 is odd. 1 is also an odd factor of every even number.
(b): False. 3 is odd, and 3 × 2 = 6 is a multiple of 3 that is even.

(c): True. If an even number were a factor of an odd number, the odd number would be a multiple of an even number, and every multiple of an even number is even. The factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15 and of 21 are 1, 3, 7, 21: all odd.
(d): True. Take 4 and 5: 4 × 5 = 20, and 20 is a multiple of 4 and of 5. Take 8 and 9: 8 × 9 = 72, a multiple of both. A product is always a multiple of the numbers multiplied.

(e): True. The factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, 8 and of 9 are 1, 3, 9: only 1 is common. The factors of 14 are 1, 2, 7, 14 and of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15: only 1 is common. A jump bigger than 1 lands on a number and then at least 2 steps further, so it cannot land on both a number and the next number.
(f): True. A jump of 0 steps stays at 0 for ever, so it can never reach a number. 0 × any number is 0, so 0 only makes the number 0.
Check: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so 3 does divide 12, and 3 × 2 = 6 is even.

items.question: Sher Khan, the tiger, goes hunting every 3rd day. Bagheera, the panther, goes hunting every 5th day. If both of them start on the same day, on which days will they be hunting together?
steps: Count the day they start together as day 0, like the start of a number line.
Sher Khan hunts on days 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, and so on: the multiples of 3.
Bagheera hunts on days 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, and so on: the multiples of 5.
Both hunt on days 15, 30, 45 and so on. These are the common multiples of 3 and 5, and the first is day 15 (3 × 5 = 15).
items.answer: On days 15, 30, 45, 60 and so on, the common multiples of 3 and 5, after the day they start together.

videos.answer: On days 15, 30, 45, 60 and so on, the common multiples of 3 and 5, after the day they start together.

items.question: (a): In the trail shown earlier, Sher Khan's house is on number 25 and that of Baloo the bear is on number 30. Mowgli wants to meet his friend Baloo the bear but wants to avoid Sher Khan's house. How long (in steps) could each jump be? (b): What number of jumps (in steps) he could choose so that he can meet both Kaa, the snake, at 21 and Akela, the wolf, at 35?
steps: (a): a jump meets Baloo at 30 when the jump size is a factor of 30. The factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30.
A jump avoids Sher Khan at 25 when the jump size is not a factor of 25. The factors of 25 are 1, 5, 25.
Take out the jump sizes that land on 25: 1 (1 × 25 = 25) and 5 (5 × 5 = 25).
The jumps that meet Baloo and avoid Sher Khan are 2, 3, 6, 10, 15 and 30 steps.
(b): the jump must be a common factor of 21 and 35. The factors of 21 are 1, 3, 7, 21 and of 35 are 1, 5, 7, 35. Common: 1 and 7.
Check: 7 × 3 = 21 and 7 × 5 = 35. Also 6 × 5 = 30, and jumps of 6 go 24 then 30, skipping 25.
items.answer: (a): 2, 3, 6, 10, 15 or 30 steps. (b): 1 or 7 steps.

videos.answer: (a): 2, 3, 6, 10, 15 or 30 steps. (b): 1 or 7 steps.

items.question: Sort the following numbers into those that are (a): divisible by 2 only (b): divisible by 5 only (c): divisible by 10 only (d): divisible by 2, 5, and 10. 90, 22, 38, 30, 75, 45, 66, 78, 62, 40, 84, 56, 25, 95, 55
steps: A number is divisible by 2 when 2 is a factor of it. The same is true for 5 and for 10.
90: 90 ÷ 2 = 45, 90 ÷ 5 = 18 and 90 ÷ 10 = 9, all exact. 90 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10.
22, 38, 66, 78, 62, 84 and 56 are divisible by 2 but not by 5 (for example 22 ÷ 2 = 11, but 5 × 4 = 20 and 5 × 5 = 25 skip 22). So these 7 are divisible by 2 only.
75, 45, 25, 95 and 55 are divisible by 5 but not by 2, because they are odd (for example 45 ÷ 5 = 9). So these 5 are divisible by 5 only.
No number is divisible by 10 only: a number divisible by 10 is also divisible by 2 and 5 (10 = 2 × 5), so 90, 30 and 40 go in the middle.
Check: 7 + 5 + 3 = 15, the same as the number of cards.
